complexity.notes: int(a/b) converts through a float, which can lose precision or raise OverflowError for very large intermediate products (possible in theory given the constraints); a pure-integer truncating division such as (abs(a)//abs(b)) * (1 if (a<0)==(b<0) else -1) would be safer. Minor style point: chained if/elif on operator strings is fine, but a dict mapping operators to lambdas would be more idiomatic.
complexity.summary: Classic stack-based RPN evaluation: push operands, and on each operator pop two values, apply the operation, and push the result. Handles subtraction/division operand order explicitly and truncates division toward zero.
